name: Kakadu and the Top End
tagline: A vast tropical wilderness of wetlands, escarpments, waterfalls and some of the world's oldest rock art, in the heart of Bininj/Mungguy country and home to saltwater crocodiles.
highlight: Sunset from Ubirr, looking over the floodplains after a walk past thousands of years of rock art.
shortDescription: Australia's largest national park, a UNESCO site for both nature and culture, with Ubirr and Nourlangie rock art, Yellow Water cruises, Jim Jim Falls and Litchfield, reached from Darwin.
metaDescription: A Kakadu and Top End travel guide: Ubirr and Nourlangie rock art, Yellow Water cruise, Jim Jim and Twin Falls, Litchfield National Park, Darwin, crocodile safety, dry and wet seasons and a four-day plan.
knownFor: Rock art, wetlands, waterfalls, crocodiles, Aboriginal culture
goodFor: Aboriginal culture, wildlife, birdwatching, waterfalls, adventure

image.alt: The Yellow Water billabong at Kakadu National Park with wetlands and water lilies

intro: Kakadu National Park, in the Northern Territory, is the largest national park in Australia, covering about 20,000 square kilometres, an area nearly the size of Wales. It is on the UNESCO World Heritage List for both its natural and its cultural values, one of the few places in the world to hold a dual listing. It is jointly managed by its Aboriginal traditional owners, the Bininj/Mungguy, and Parks Australia.

The landscape ranges from tidal flats and floodplains to billabongs, lowland forest and the stone country of the Arnhem Land escarpment. It is home to more than 280 bird species, huge numbers of saltwater crocodiles, and rock art galleries at Ubirr, Nourlangie and other sites that record thousands of years of human occupation, and some of them are among the oldest in the world. Aboriginal people have lived here for at least 65,000 years.

The Top End has two seasons: the dry, from May to October, and the wet, from November to April. Most visitors come in the dry, when the roads are open, the weather is warm and sunny and the waterfalls are accessible, though the falls run best early in the season. The wet brings flooding, closed roads, dramatic storms and green landscapes for those who are prepared. Darwin, the regional capital, is the gateway.

whyVisit.intro: Kakadu is one of the most remarkable places in Australia, both for its wildlife and its cultural heritage.

points.title: Ancient rock art
points.text: Galleries at Ubirr and Nourlangie, with paintings that span tens of thousands of years.

points.title: Wetlands and wildlife
points.text: Boat cruises on Yellow Water spot crocodiles, jabirus, sea eagles and thousands of waterbirds.

points.title: Waterfalls and gorges
points.text: Jim Jim and Twin Falls tumble off the escarpment in the early dry season.

points.title: Living culture
points.text: Aboriginal-led tours and cultural centres share stories and knowledge.

attractionsIntro: The main sights are spread across a huge park, so plan a route and a few nights of accommodation.

attractions.name: Ubirr Rock Art

image.file: File:Kakadu (AU), Kakadu National Park, Ubirr Rock Art -- 2019 -- 4169.jpg
image.alt: Aboriginal rock art paintings on a sandstone wall at Ubirr in Kakadu

attractions.text: A rock outcrop in the north of the park with galleries of paintings of fish, animals and figures, and a climb to a lookout over the floodplains, one of the best sunset views in Australia.
attractions.tip: Go in the late afternoon, and stay for sunset.

attractions.name: Nourlangie (Burrungkuy)

image.alt: The sandstone outlier of Nourlangie Rock in Kakadu National Park

attractions.text: A sandstone outlier with shelters decorated with rock art, including some paintings of spirit beings, and a lookout at Nawurlandja.
attractions.tip: Read the interpretive signs, which tell of the creation stories.

attractions.name: Yellow Water (Ngurrungurrlba) Billabong
attractions.text: A wetland on the South Alligator River floodplain, explored by boat at sunrise or late afternoon, with crocodiles, jabirus, whistling ducks and water lilies.

attractions.name: Jim Jim and Twin Falls

image.file: File:Kakadu (AU), Kakadu National Park, Jim Jim Creek -- 2019 -- 4240.jpg
image.alt: The rocky gorge and creek at Jim Jim in Kakadu National Park

attractions.text: Waterfalls that plunge over the escarpment, reached by a 4WD track and a walk, and open only in the dry season when the track is passable. Swimming may be prohibited if crocodiles are present.
attractions.tip: Check road and swimming conditions with park rangers.

attractions.name: Warradjan Aboriginal Cultural Centre
attractions.text: A centre in the shape of a pig-nosed turtle, with displays about the Bininj/Mungguy culture, art and stories.
attractions.tip: Visit early in your trip for context.

attractions.name: Litchfield National Park

image.alt: Wangi Falls tumbling into a plunge pool in Litchfield National Park

attractions.text: A smaller park about 1.5 hours south of Darwin, with waterfalls and swimming holes at Wangi Falls and Florence Falls, and giant termite mounds. A good option for a day trip.

thingsToDoIntro: Kakadu is about culture, wildlife and time outdoors.

thingsToDo.title: See the rock art at Ubirr
thingsToDo.text: Walk a short trail past painted shelters, and climb for the view.
thingsToDo.tip: Go with a ranger talk if available.

thingsToDo.title: Cruise Yellow Water
thingsToDo.text: A boat trip at dawn among crocodiles and birds.

thingsToDo.title: Take an Aboriginal-led tour
thingsToDo.text: Local guides share knowledge of bush foods, fishing and rock art.
thingsToDo.tip: Choose operators owned by Traditional Owners.

thingsToDo.title: Swim at a safe pool
thingsToDo.text: Some waterholes are monitored and safe for swimming, such as Maguk and Gunlom, when open.

thingsToDo.title: Watch birds
thingsToDo.text: Kakadu is one of Australia's best birding areas.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Darwin's markets
thingsToDo.text: The Mindil Beach Sunset Market has food, crafts and sunsets in the dry season.
thingsToDo.tip: It runs on Thursday and Sunday evenings.

foodIntro: Food in Kakadu is simple, with barramundi and barbecue, and Darwin has a lively multicultural scene.

foods.name: Barramundi
foods.text: The northern fish, served grilled, battered or in a curry.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and pubs across the Top End.

foods.name: Buffalo and crocodile
foods.text: Local meats served at outback pubs and barbecues.

foods.name: Laksa and Asian food
foods.text: Darwin's food reflects its links with Southeast Asia, with excellent laksa and satay.

foods.name: Bush tucker
foods.text: Native fruit, honey and herbs, such as Kakadu plum, one of the richest sources of vitamin C in the world.

foods.name: Tropical fruit
foods.text: Mangoes, from October, and other fruit.

accommodation.intro: Accommodation in the park is limited and should be booked ahead, particularly in the dry season.

areas.name: Jabiru
areas.text: The park's main town, with hotels and a caravan park.

areas.name: Cooinda and Yellow Water
areas.text: A lodge and campground near the billabong.

areas.name: Darwin
areas.text: A wide range of hotels and restaurants.

budget.label: Park pass
budget.value: About A$40 per adult, valid for a week

gettingThere.intro: Kakadu is about 250 km east of Darwin.

options.text: About 2.5 to 3 hours to Jabiru or Cooinda, on sealed roads. 4WD is needed for some tracks, such as Jim Jim.
options.detail: Book early in the dry season.

options.text: Day tours and multi-day trips leave Darwin.
Direct flights from Sydney, Melbourne, Perth and Asian cities.
options.detail: The airport is near the city.

gettingAround.intro: Distances within the park are long, and roads can flood.

options.detail: Carry fuel and water, and check road conditions.

options.text: Guided trips remove the driving stress.
Cruises on Yellow Water and the East Alligator River.

bestTime.headline: May–October
bestTime.summary: The dry season is best, with warm days and low humidity. The wet season from November to April brings storms, flooding and closed roads.

seasons.text: Green, with waterfalls at their best and cooler weather.
Hot, dry and dusty, with wildlife concentrating at water.
Extreme humidity, flooding and closed roads, but dramatic and green.

bestTime.avoid: The wet season, unless you are prepared for closures and heat.

itinerary.title: Four days in Kakadu
itinerary.intro: From Darwin into the park, with rock art, a cruise and waterfalls.

tipsIntro: Safety and respect matter in Kakadu.
tips: Never swim in water not marked safe. Saltwater crocodiles are present in rivers, billabongs and some waterholes.
Check the park website and road conditions for closures.
Buy a park pass in advance.
Follow the rules about sacred sites and photography.
Carry plenty of water, and wear sunscreen and insect repellent.
Book accommodation and cruises well ahead in the dry season.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Kakadu?
faq.a: Three days at least, and four or five for a relaxed visit.
Only at designated safe swimming areas. Saltwater crocodiles are common in the park.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: May to October, the dry season.
Not for the main sights, but some tracks, such as Jim Jim Falls, require one.
Yes, if you follow the warning signs, especially about crocodiles, and stay hydrated.

faq.q: Can I visit as a day trip from Darwin?
faq.a: It is possible on a long day tour, but three days is much better.
